results.content: President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen 14 percentage points among Republicans since April of last year, while only a quarter of respondents approve of his handling of the Iran war, according to a new poll. Aug. 31Trump’s approval rating has decreased one point, to 32%, since March, and his disapproval rating has increased two points, to 64%, according to a University of Massachusetts Amherst poll of 1,000 respondents taken Aug. 21-26 (margin of error 3.5). results.content: President Trump’s approval rating has remained stagnant at the lowest point between his two presidencies, according to a new poll. The latest Reuters/Ipsos survey shows that Trump’s approval rating has remained at 33 percent — the third time the pollsters have found this result — amid the unpopularity of the Iran war and rising prices. The same poll found that 71 percent of respondents said they do not approve of Trump’s handling of the cost of living, which has become one of the top issues for voters during this primary election season and beyond. A plurality of voters, at 47 percent, said the cost of living would be the most important factor in deciding whom to support in November. Registe

results.content: His favorable rating rose to 40 percent while his unfavorable rating fell to 50 percent, narrowing his net deficit from 12 points in July to 10 points in August, the latest I&I/TIPP survey shows. Key Points Why It Matters Trump appears to have recovered some of the ground lost during an early-summer decline, when his net favorability reached minus 16 points in June. Favorability Moves in Trump’s Direction The I&I/TIPP Poll, published August 31, found that 40 percent of adults held a favorable opinion of Trump and 50 percent viewed him unfavorably.
